The Lernaean Hydra. A serpentine monstrosity with nine heads—eight mortal and one immortal—that terrorized the marshes of Lerna in Argos. Slaying this monster formed the second labor of Heracles, who discovered that cutting off one head caused two more to grow back, forcing him to employ both fire and cleverness to finally defeat it. One of the nine heads was immortal and could not be killed by ordinary means, requiring special treatment to permanently defeat it.

Each head regrew as two new heads whenever one was severed, making straightforward combat increasingly hopeless. The creature's breath and blood were so venomous that the very fumes could kill a man, and its fangs dripped with lethal poison. Heracles eventually realized he needed to sear each neck stump with fire to prevent regeneration while attacking the immortal head. The immortal head was buried under a massive rock after being severed, keeping it permanently imprisoned.

The monster's parents were usually said to be Echidna and Typhon, making it kin to other legendary beasts like the Chimera. Its lair in the Lernaean marshes was so mephitic that simply approaching it could sicken a traveler. The second labor was considered far more challenging than the first—the Nemean Lion—pushing Heracles to use intellect alongside brute strength.
